session_label: Aegis PMA · for Mon 9 Nov 2026 · AQE data to COB Fri 6 Nov

bottom_line.headline: Three contested breakout buys into a risk-off tape, with a flat book and nothing to defend.
bottom_line.paragraph: BILL, CHYM and KO advance, but none is agreed: each carries an open objection, and the VIV System's doctrine on a risk-off read is to build the watchlist, not push new entries. VIX at 25.6 sits above the already-priced mark of 25 and SPY is 2.89 daily ranges under its 50-day average, the state one decider says voids every buy: a market note with no printed level, not an alert.

weather.text: A broad market with protection already expensive. Status is degraded: the whole-market breadth leg was unreachable, so the read rests on the equal-weight ratio, volatility, dealer and positioning legs.

Stance RISK OFF: SPY below its short-term averages on daily and weekly charts. The handbook's doctrine is to build the watchlist and not push new entries, quoted as the VIV System's rule, not an Aegis sizing rule.
RED light: SPY 735.29 is 3.75% under the 762.89 level where dealers stop amplifying moves, so swings run larger than the news in both directions.
This tape pays patience, not breakouts: the three advances are buy-on-trigger names, and a trigger that does not print is a name to watch, not a soft buy.

weather.stance: Read: Valen's stance is RISK OFF, down from NEUTRAL five days ago and a month ago. SPY and QQQ fail the daily and weekly buy tests and neither is above a rising 5-day average; SPY sits 2.89 and QQQ 4.2 average daily ranges below their 50-day averages, a downtrend rather than a stretch. VIX over its 3-month contract is 1.04, above the 1.00 stress mark (0.93 five days ago). The handbook's doctrine: build the watchlist, do not push new entries; that is the VIV System's rule, not an Aegis sizing rule.
weather.gex: Read: the light is RED. SPY at 735.29 is 3.75% under 762.89, the level where dealers stop amplifying moves, so expect bigger swings than the news deserves in both directions. The heaviest put strike, 740, is already above Friday's close, so that cushion is not underneath; the heaviest call strike is 750 and rallies into it tend to meet selling. Reclaiming about 763 is what calms the tape. Who holds which side is an assumed convention, not observed data.
weather.heartbeat: Read: the average stock has kept up with the index for 15 sessions (broadening), with the equal-weight ratio up 1.7% over 5 days, 7.4% over 20 and 2.6% over 60. It sits near the top of its 12-month range, 1.69% under the high, which Crown reads as late in the phase rather than early. The phase ends on a cross below its 20-day average at 0.284, 3.35% under today. Read confidence 0.75; the gate passed, so the rest of the read ran.
weather.positioning: Read: trend-following funds are neutral across 18 markets, none at an extreme, size dial 1.00; their leanings are long the dollar (+0.47) and short rates (-0.27). The nearest turns are close and on the buy side: the Russell 2000 above 2,787.55 (0.27% away) and the S&P above 7,443.89 (0.28% away) turn them from sellers to buyers. On the sell side they turn sellers of the Dow below 50,622 (2.05% lower) and of crude below 88.17 (2.21% lower). For a momentum book a small push up turns these funds into buyers, which would help any breakout that triggers.
weather.volatility: Read: VIX 25.64 is higher than 94% of days in the past two years and above the 25 already-priced mark, so protection is expensive, not cheap. Single stocks are implied at 47.42, a gap of 21.78 over the index that is higher than 66% of its history, inside the normal band and narrowing (down 2.32 in 20 days). Implied correlation is 20.76 and the volatility curve is inverted, near-term above longer-term, the stress shape. The file warns that two cross-checks disagree with the gap, so read it with caution.
weather.divergence: Read: one warning is lit at market level, momentum not keeping up with price, and 7 more show on individual markets. Breadth does not confirm it: the average stock is still keeping up with the index. No single sign is a reason to sell; they matter when several point the same way as breadth, and today they do not.
weather.call: Read: Crown's mechanical family is broadening carry (own the average stock, collect premium against it) at a partial fit: the range-not-extreme and positive-dealer-gamma conditions both fail. The size multiplier is 1.00x the PM's own risk; on the fund file's 1R of $620 that is $620, arithmetic only. The leading macro story is a growth scare with 81% of its conditions met at full coverage, not contested; the runner-up is a dollar squeeze. Next scheduled test: CPI on Tuesday 10 Nov at 08:30 ET (21:30 SGT).
weather.cot: Read: big speculators are crowded long the Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000 small caps, the long bond and the 5-year and 2-year notes, and crowded short crude, natural gas and silver. The report covers Tuesday 3 Nov, published Friday; the next is 13 Nov. For equities the Nasdaq and small-cap longs are the crowding that matters: it is context, never timing, but a break would force that same money out fast.
weather.checklist: Read: today's 4% count is green, but the 5-day count is 0.33 against 1.00 to pass and net new highs fail (8-day average 17.12 under the 20-day 22.8); monthly big risers are 90. Stocks above their 40-day average: 46%; above the 20-, 50- and 200-day: 44%, 42.3% and 42.1%. These come from the dashboard's own population, US-listed stocks over $2B (3,748 names), not from AQE's list and not the full tape the handbook assumes. Net new highs failing puts the handbook's trade-management switch on the tighten side.
weather.turning: Read: stance RISK OFF now, NEUTRAL five days ago and a month ago; trend DOWNTREND now and five days ago, CHOP a month ago; stocks above their 40-day average 46% now, 53.9% five days ago, 27.3% a month ago; VIX over its 3-month contract 1.04, 0.93 and 0.85. To turn positive the handbook wants the 40-day share above 50% (now 46%) and the 5-day count above 1.00 (now 0.33); the 5-day count already sits under the 0.70 negative mark. The handbook's monthly-risers threshold is a whole-market count and is not cited as reachable here.
weather.themes: Read: on both the week and month lists, real leadership: Gold Miners, Solar Renewables, MedTech, Gaming Streaming, Homebuilders. Leading from near their own highs, not bouncing: E-Commerce (3.5% off its high), REITs (3.7%), Insurance (4.2%), Biotech (2.5%). Strong numbers but well off their highs, a bounce rather than leadership: Gold Miners (24.5% off), Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Software, Payments (16.1% off). The violent turns are inside broken groups, Quantum Computing (61% off its high), Chip Equipment (48.6%), Crypto (55%): not leadership.
weather.groups: Read: the turning sectors are Technology, Industrials and Communication Services, all graded turning and recovering from weakness; the room's strongest names in them are STGW and MGNI (Communication Services), ADP (Industrials) and BILL and TOST (Technology). Healthcare, Staples and Real Estate are further along, already leading and still strengthening, with CAH, BDX, KO, CHD, EL, AHR and JAN among their names. This is a place to look, not a list to buy.

BILL.case: Contested buy: the best-built base on the list and a market leader; the open objection wants the pullback to the rising 20-day average instead of the break, and that pullback would clear it.

reason.agree: The strongest base on the list, a market leader whose advance is speeding up on heavier-than-normal volume, and not yet stretched past where it broke out.
reason.wrong_if: Wrong if it falls back under the level it broke out from on heavy volume, or the payments group fails to make new highs with it.
reason.wait_for: Wait for an hourly close above 53.73 on volume at least 1.4 times normal; that sits just above the room's own too-late mark of 53.30.

plan: Before the 22:30 SGT open: nothing is held and no stop needs setting; the three buy levels are BILL above 53.73, CHYM above 32.08 and KO above 96.31, each on an hourly close, not a touch.
At the open: dealers amplify moves while SPY is under 762.89, so a gap through a buy level is noise until the first hourly close at 23:30 SGT.
First hour: check the volume on any break; BILL and CHYM need at least 1.4 times normal, and KO has no written level, so set that bar before it trades.

Plan-changers: S&P futures above 7,443.89 or the Russell 2000 above 2,787.55 turn trend funds into buyers and help any break; the equal-weight ratio under its 20-day average at 0.284 ends the broad-market read.
Into the close: a daily close back under the breakout level ends each case (BILL 50.76, CHYM 31.07, KO 95.37); CPI prints Tuesday at 21:30 SGT, before the next session opens.

Book is flat: the export's held positions are empty and the 5 and 6 Nov journals show no open positions; the Tiger options-wheel stock lines (including KO) are outside this committee's book.
The data check first failed on held-position health fields that a flat book does not carry; it was fixed at source and re-reads healthy.
The market kill is named by one decider only and carries no level: a market note, not an alert.
